data.name: Tray_Tooltip_NoDevice
data.comment: Tray icon tooltip before any device state exists (demo build start-up). One line; the whole tooltip is cut at 127 characters by Windows.

data.name: Tray_Tooltip_DeviceNameDemo
data.comment: Device name as shown in the tray tooltip while the demo transport is active. {0} = device name, e.g. "AirPods Pro". Part of a tooltip of at most 127 characters.

data.name: Tray_Tooltip_BatteryLevelStale
data.comment: One battery level in the tray tooltip when the reading is old. {0} = percent text, e.g. "85%"; {1} = how old it is, e.g. "last seen 5 min ago". Keep short: the tooltip is cut at 127 characters.

data.name: Tray_Tooltip_SingleBattery
data.comment: Tray tooltip for a device with one battery (e.g. AirPods Max). {0} = device name, {1} = connection state sentence fragment such as "Connected", {2} = battery level, e.g. "85%". The whole tooltip is cut at 127 characters.

data.name: Tray_Tooltip_EarbudsBattery
data.comment: Tray tooltip for earbuds. {0} = device name, {1} = connection state such as "Connected", {2} = left earbud level, {3} = right earbud level (e.g. "85%"). "L" and "R" mean left and right earbud. The whole tooltip is cut at 127 characters.

data.name: Tray_Menu_WindowsBattery
data.comment: Disabled first line of the tray menu, battery as reported by Windows. {0} = device noun such as "AirPods" or "Headphones"; {1} = percent number (no % sign). One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_NearbySingle
data.comment: Tray menu info line for a one-battery device, estimated from nearby Bluetooth broadcasts. {0} = percent text, e.g. "85%". One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_NearbySingleStale
data.comment: Tray menu info line for a one-battery device when the estimate is old. {0} = age, e.g. "5 min ago"; {1} = percent text, e.g. "85%". One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_NearbyEarbuds
data.comment: Tray menu info line for earbuds, estimated from nearby broadcasts. {0} = left level, {1} = right level (e.g. "85%"), {2} = optional case section (empty, or the text of Tray_Menu_NearbyCase / Tray_Menu_NearbyCaseStale). "L"/"R" = left/right earbud. One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_NearbyEarbudsStale
data.comment: Tray menu info line for earbuds when the estimate is old. {0} = age, e.g. "5 min ago"; {1} = left level, {2} = right level; {3} = optional case section (empty, or Tray_Menu_NearbyCase / Tray_Menu_NearbyCaseStale). One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_NearbyCase
data.comment: Case section appended to the tray menu earbuds line; keep the leading separator and space. {0} = charging case level, e.g. "85%".

data.name: Tray_Menu_NearbyCaseStale
data.comment: Case section appended to the tray menu earbuds line when the case reading is old; keep the leading separator and space. {0} = case level, e.g. "85%"; {1} = age, e.g. "last seen 5 min ago".

data.name: Tray_Menu_BatteryUnavailable
data.comment: Disabled first line of the tray menu when no battery level is known. One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_BatteryUnavailableHandsfreeOff
data.comment: Disabled first line of the tray menu when no battery level is known because the Bluetooth Handsfree profile is off. "Handsfree" is the Windows Bluetooth profile name. One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_ConnectAirPods
data.comment: Tray menu item that connects the selected AirPods. Menu item, one line (may be shown greyed out).

data.name: Tray_Menu_DisconnectAirPods
data.comment: Tray menu item that disconnects the connected AirPods. Menu item, one line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_Connecting
data.comment: Greyed-out tray menu item while a connection attempt is running. One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_Disconnecting
data.comment: Greyed-out tray menu item while a disconnect is running. One line.

data.name: Tray_Menu_Open
data.comment: Tray menu item that opens the flyout. "&" marks the keyboard accelerator letter; keep exactly one and make it unique among the menu items (Open, Settings, Quit). Keep "Clasp" untranslated.

data.name: Tray_Menu_Settings
data.comment: Tray menu item that opens the Settings window. "&" marks the keyboard accelerator letter; keep exactly one, unique among the menu items.

data.name: Tray_Menu_Quit
data.comment: Tray menu item that quits Clasp. "&" marks the keyboard accelerator letter; keep exactly one, unique among the menu items.

data.name: Toast_UpdateAvailable_Title
data.comment: Windows toast notification title when a new Clasp version is found. {0} = version number, e.g. "0.4.3". One line (about 40 characters visible).

data.name: Toast_UpdateAvailable_Body
data.value: Open Clasp from the tray to update.
data.comment: Windows toast notification body under Toast_UpdateAvailable_Title. One or two lines.

data.name: Toast_CrashNotice_Title
data.comment: Windows toast notification title shown at the next start after Clasp crashed. One line (about 40 characters visible).

data.name: Toast_CrashNotice_Body
data.value: Sorry about that. If it keeps happening, the log is hub.log in {0}. It has no device names, and you can attach it to a bug report.

data.name: Hotkey_Problem_AlreadyAssigned
data.value: Already assigned to another Clasp action.
data.comment: Problem text under a keyboard shortcut field in Settings: the same key combination is already used by a different Clasp action. One short sentence, may wrap to 2 lines.

data.name: Hotkey_Problem_UsedByOtherProgram
data.value: Another program already uses this shortcut.
data.comment: Problem text under a keyboard shortcut field in Settings: Windows reports the combination is taken by another program. One short sentence, may wrap.

data.name: Hotkey_Problem_WindowsRefused
data.comment: Problem text under a keyboard shortcut field in Settings when Windows rejected the combination. {0} = Windows' own error description (already in the user's Windows language). May wrap.

data.name: Hotkey_Problem_ShortcutsUnavailable
data.comment: Problem text under each assigned keyboard shortcut in Settings when shortcuts could not be set up at all. One short sentence, may wrap.

data.name: UpdateReason_DownloadTooLarge

data.name: UpdateReason_DownloadIncomplete
data.comment: Lower-case clause completing "Clasp didn't install the update because ...". Starts mid-sentence; ends with a period.

data.name: UpdateReason_WrongSize

data.comment: Lower-case clause completing "Clasp didn't install the update because ...". Starts mid-sentence; ends with a period.

data.name: UpdateReason_SignatureMismatch
data.value: its signature doesn't match Clasp's release key.

data.name: UpdateReason_FolderNotPlain

data.comment: Lower-case clause completing "Clasp didn't install the update because ...". Starts mid-sentence; ends with a period.

data.name: UpdateReason_SignatureTooLarge

data.comment: Lower-case clause completing "Clasp didn't install the update because ...". Starts mid-sentence; ends with a period.

data.name: UpdateReason_InstallerNoLongerVerified

data.name: CompHost_Links_On
data.value: Links are on. Open clasp://connect to try one.
data.comment: Status under the "Allow clasp:// links" toggle in Settings when the clasp:// link handler is registered. Keep "clasp://connect" as is. One or two lines.

data.name: CompHost_Links_CouldntTurnOn
data.value: Couldn't turn on links. clasp:// links won't open Clasp.
data.comment: Status under the "Allow clasp:// links" toggle in Settings when registering the link handler failed. Keep "clasp://" as is. One or two lines.

data.name: CompHost_Handsfree_CheckingMicrophone
data.value: Checking whether your microphone is in use…
data.comment: Status line under the Handsfree option (Smart mode) in Settings while the microphone state is being read. One line.

data.name: CompHost_Handsfree_NoAddress
data.value: Couldn't find your AirPods to change Handsfree. Clasp left it as it was.
data.comment: Status line under the Handsfree option in Settings when the Bluetooth address of the selected AirPods is unknown. "Handsfree" = Bluetooth Handsfree profile (calls/microphone mode). Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: CompHost_Handsfree_AccessDenied
data.value: Windows needs administrator access to change Handsfree. Clasp left it as it was.
data.comment: Status line under the Handsfree option in Settings when Windows denied the change. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: CompHost_Handsfree_DeviceNotFound
data.value: Windows couldn't find these AirPods. Clasp left Handsfree as it was.
data.comment: Status line under the Handsfree option in Settings when Windows could not find the device. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: CompHost_Handsfree_Failed
data.comment: Status line under the Handsfree option in Settings when the change failed. {0} = Windows error number.

data.name: CompHost_Handsfree_Blocked
data.value: {0} Clasp left it as it was.
data.comment: Status line under the Handsfree option in Settings when Clasp stopped trying. {0} = a full sentence explaining why (from another resource, ends with a period).

data.name: CompHost_LowLatency_On
data.comment: Status next to the "Low audio latency" setting in Settings when the feature is running. One or two words.

data.name: CompHost_LowLatency_WaitingForConnect
data.value: Waiting for your AirPods to connect
data.comment: Status next to the "Low audio latency" setting while the AirPods are not connected. One line.

data.name: CompHost_LowLatency_WaitingForOutput
data.value: Waiting for Windows to show your AirPods
data.comment: Status next to the "Low audio latency" setting while Windows has not yet listed the AirPods as a sound output. One line.

data.name: CompHost_LowLatency_NotDefaultOutput
data.value: Paused. Your AirPods aren't the sound output.
data.comment: Status next to the "Low audio latency" setting when the AirPods are connected but another device is the sound output. One or two lines.

data.name: CompHost_LowLatency_Retrying
data.comment: Status next to the "Low audio latency" setting after a failed start, before the next retry. One line.

data.name: CompHost_LowLatency_Stopped
data.comment: Status next to the "Low audio latency" setting after repeated failures. One line.

data.name: CompHost_Stem_HookUnavailable
data.value: Clasp can't watch for stem presses, so stem actions are off.
data.comment: Status under the "Stem actions" toggle in Settings when the keyboard hook could not start. "Stem" = the stem (stalk) of an AirPod. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: CompHost_Stem_Waiting
data.value: Waiting for a stem press. If this doesn't change when you press the stem, stem actions may not work on this PC.
data.comment: Status under the "Stem actions" toggle in Settings before any stem press has been seen. Wraps to 2-3 lines.

data.name: CompHost_Stem_HeardOne
data.value: Heard {0} stem press since this was turned on.
data.comment: Status under the "Stem actions" toggle in Settings when exactly one press was seen. {0} = the number 1. Wraps to 2 lines. The plural form is CompHost_Stem_HeardMany.

data.name: CompHost_Stem_HeardMany
data.value: Heard {0} stem presses since this was turned on.
data.comment: Status under the "Stem actions" toggle in Settings when several presses were seen. {0} = the count (2 or more). Wraps to 2 lines. The singular form is CompHost_Stem_HeardOne.

data.name: CompHost_PerApp_CheckFailed
data.value: Couldn't check whether this PC supports per-app output.
data.comment: Status under the "Per-app output" setting in Settings when the support check threw an error. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: CompHost_Repair_ChooseDevice
data.value: Choose your AirPods in Settings first.
data.comment: Result line of the "Fix connection" button in Settings when no AirPods are selected. One line.

data.name: CompHost_Repair_Stopped
data.value: Fix connection stopped. Make sure Bluetooth is on in Windows Settings.
data.comment: Result line of the "Fix connection" button in Settings after an unexpected error. "Windows Settings" is the Windows Settings app. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: WinAudio_UnnamedOutput
data.comment: Name used in the sound output lists in Settings for a Windows audio output that has no name. Shown as a list item label, one line.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_CouldntSwitchBack
data.value: Couldn't switch back. Nothing was changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings after Clasp tried to return sound to the previous output with invalid input. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_RequestExpired
data.value: That request expired. Nothing was changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when the automatic switch-back request was overtaken by newer events.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_OutputChangedKept
data.value: The output changed, so your newer choice was kept.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when the user (or Windows) changed the sound output before Clasp's switch-back, so Clasp did nothing.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_AirPodsStillConnected
data.value: Your AirPods are still connected. Nothing was changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when a switch-back was skipped because the AirPods are still connected.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_PreviousUnavailable
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when the output to return to is missing or disconnected.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_AlreadyPrevious
data.value: Sound is already going to the previous output.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when sound already plays on the output that Clasp would switch back to.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_PreviousUnavailableNothingChanged
data.value: The previous output isn't available. Nothing was changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when the output to return to disappeared just before the switch.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_DevicesChanged
data.value: Your audio devices changed. Nothing was changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when audio devices changed while Clasp was about to switch back.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_NotConfirmed
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when Windows did not confirm the switch back.

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_Switched
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings after a successful automatic switch back. {0} = output device name, e.g. "Speakers (Realtek Audio)".

data.name: WinAudio_Restore_Failed
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when the switch back failed. {0} = Windows error code in hexadecimal; keep "0x{0:X8}" as is.

data.name: WinAudio_Output_ChooseFirst
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when "Use this output" was pressed with no output chosen.

data.name: WinAudio_Output_Disconnected
data.value: That output is disconnected, so nothing was changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when the chosen output is not connected.

data.name: WinAudio_Output_DisconnectedPartway
data.value: The output disconnected partway. Some settings may already have changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when the output disappeared while Clasp was changing the Windows default. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: WinAudio_Output_NotConfirmed
data.value: Windows didn't confirm the change. Some settings may already have changed.
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when Windows did not confirm the new default output. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: WinAudio_Output_Switched
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings after the user chose an output. {0} = output device name, e.g. "Speakers (Realtek Audio)".

data.name: WinAudio_Output_SwitchFailed
data.comment: Audio output status line in Settings when Windows rejected the change of the default output.

data.name: WinAudio_Volume_Invalid
data.comment: Volume status line in Settings when the requested volume is out of range.

data.name: WinAudio_Volume_OutputDisconnected
data.value: That output is disconnected, so its volume wasn't changed.
data.comment: Volume status line in Settings when the output is not connected.

data.name: WinAudio_Volume_ReadbackDiffers
data.value: Volume changed, but Windows reports about {0}%.
data.comment: Volume status line in Settings when the volume read back differs from the requested one. {0} = percent number (no % sign).

data.name: WinAudio_Volume_Changed
data.comment: Volume status line in Settings after a successful change. {0} = output device name, {1} = percent number (no % sign).

data.name: WinAudio_Volume_ChangeFailed
data.comment: Volume status line in Settings when Windows rejected the volume change.

data.name: WinPerApp_Support_NotCheckedYet
data.comment: Support detail for per-app output before the check ran. Rarely shown. One line.

data.name: WinPerApp_Support_NotAvailable
data.value: Per-app output isn't available on this PC.

data.name: WinPerApp_Support_WindowsVersionUnsupported
data.value: This version of Windows doesn't support per-app output.

data.name: WinPerApp_Support_SafetyCheckFailed

data.name: WinPerApp_Support_Available
data.value: Available. This relies on an experimental Windows feature.
data.comment: Support detail for per-app output when it can be used. Wraps to 2 lines.

data.name: WinConn_CanceledBeforeRequest
